root_cause.text: mddev_suspend() in the md RAID456 path killed active_io and waited for it to drain without waking I/O blocked in raid5_make_request() on wait_for_reshape, so frozen/interrupted reshape left those requests holding active_io forever and caused a suspend deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that direct I/O “can sleep in raid5_make_request() waiting for reshape progress while still holding an active_io reference,” and the patch adds a call in mddev_suspend() to pers->prepare_suspend(mddev) when reshape_interrupted(mddev) is true specifically to “wake those waiters so they can abort and drop the reference instead of deadlocking suspend.”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states that direct I/O “can sleep in raid5_make_request() waiting for reshape progress while still holding an active_io reference,” and the patch adds a call in mddev_suspend() to pers->prepare_suspend(mddev) when reshape_interrupted(mddev) is true specifically to “wake those waiters so they can abort and drop the reference instead of deadlocking suspend.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Wake interrupted or frozen RAID reshape waiters during suspend so they can drop active_io references and avoid deadlock in mddev_suspend().
intent_record.what: After calling percpu_ref_kill(&mddev->active_io) in mddev_suspend(), the change adds a comment and a new conditional block that checks whether mddev->pers exists, mddev->pers->prepare_suspend is defined, and reshape_interrupted(mddev) is true; if so, it invokes mddev->pers->prepare_suspend(mddev) before waiting for active_io to reach zero.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when suspend is initiated and a reshape operation has already been interrupted or frozen, the code now explicitly wakes or prepares RAID personality-specific waiters before blocking on active_io draining. This allows RAID456 I/O threads stuck in wait_for_reshape while still holding active_io references to abort and release those references, preventing mddev_suspend() from deadlocking while waiting for active I/O to quiesce.

grouping_result.intent: Wake interrupted or frozen RAID reshape waiters during suspend so they can drop active_io references and avoid deadlock in mddev_suspend().

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it wakes RAID reshape waiters during suspend so blocked raid5_make_request() paths can release active_io, preventing the mddev_suspend() deadlock caused by waiting for active_io to drain without waking those waiters.

candidates.rationale: Suspend kills active_io before ensuring RAID456 reshape waiters are woken. Requests blocked in raid5_make_request() continue holding active_io references, so killing the ref first contributes directly to the deadlock.
This wait for active_io to drain is vulnerable because no wakeup is issued for I/O stuck waiting on reshape state, so suspend can block indefinitely waiting for references that can never be dropped.

vuln_statements.explanation: This kills active_io references during suspend before waking RAID456 requests blocked in raid5_make_request() on wait_for_reshape. Those blocked requests keep their active_io references indefinitely, creating the deadlock condition described in the root cause.
After killing active_io, suspend waits for the reference count to drain, but without waking reshape waiters this wait can block forever because the held active_io references cannot be released.
